why: Two differences from p3, both load-bearing. execFileSync does not invoke a shell, so shell metacharacters in datasetName stay literal argv data and cannot start a second command; and the '--' terminator stops tar from interpreting a leading dash as an option, which closes the argument-injection route that execFile alone would leave open.
proof: bench/exploits.js -> p3b submits the same metacharacter payload as p3 and asserts no marker file appears.
neighbourNote: The claim names execSync explicitly. The code under audit does not call execSync at all, which makes this case a test of whether the adjudicator reads the actual sink rather than the claim's description of it.
residualNote: execFile without the '--' terminator would leave tar argument injection open. That is why the terminator is present, and why this case is genuinely clean rather than merely differently broken.
